Definition: from G4089; acridity (especially poison), literally or figuratively:--bitterness.
BiblicalUsage: Pikria is bitterness, the poison that spreads through a heart. Paul says to put away all bitterness in Ephesians 4:31, and Hebrews 12:15 warns of a root of bitterness springing up to defile many. Peter saw Simon the sorcerer in the gall of bitterness in Acts 8:23, and Romans 3:14 says the mouth of the ungodly is full of cursing and bitterness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe bitterness is a root, not a fruit — it grows underground until it poisons everyone near it. That is why I hold that the only cure is to dig it out early, before it springs up.
